morphological_indicators.description: Circular to irregular dark purple-brown to black spots with distinct feathery, fibrillose, fringed spreading margins. No concentric bullseye rings.

symptoms: Circular dark brown to pitch-black spots (2–12 mm) with characteristic feathery, fringed, fibrillose margins
Yellow chlorotic halos develop around spots, coalescing into full leaflet chlorosis
Premature defoliation starting from the lower canes and progressing upward, leaving bare thorny canes
Raised reddish-purple blister-like cankers on immature green canes
Rose___Black_spot.causes: Ascomycete fungus Diplocarpon rosae. Ascospores and conidia germinate only when foliage remains wet for at least 6–7 hours at 18–24°C.
cultural_management: Water exclusively at the base with drip or soaker irrigation; never wet rose foliage in late afternoon or evening
Prune shrub interior canes into an open vase shape to promote rapid wind drying across the canopy
Rake, bag, and incinerate all fallen leaves and diseased canes immediately; do not compost infected rose debris
Sanitize pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between individual rose bushes
organic_remedies: Apply potassium bicarbonate (3 g/L) + horticultural oil (5 ml/L) as a curative foliar wash every 7 days
Foliar spray with biological antagonist Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Bacillus subtilis
Sulfur dusting or micronized wettable sulfur spray (avoid applying when temperatures exceed 29°C/85°F to prevent phytotoxicity)

chemical_remedies.name: Tebuconazole (e.g., Bayer Advanced Disease Control / Folicur)
chemical_remedies.role: Locally systemic triazole; halts fungal sterol biosynthesis within expanding black spot hyphae.

chemical_remedies.name: Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole (e.g., Compass Trio / Nativo)
chemical_remedies.role: Translaminar strobilurin barrier combined with systemic curative action.

ornamental_care.petal_safety: CRITICAL: Do NOT spray directly onto open rose petals or colored buds. Chemical contact causes immediate petal scorch, bleaching, and unmarketable blooms.
ornamental_care.winter_sanitation: Overwintering ascocarps survive in fallen leaf litter. Complete winter ground clean-up is mandatory before spring bud break.
ornamental_care.root_drench: Systemic triazoles can be applied as a seasonal root zone drench for non-spray protection in residential gardens.

Rose___Black_spot.tank_mix: Tank mix Tebuconazole with a non-ionic spreader/sticker to adhere to glossy rose waxy cuticles. Jar test before spraying.
Rose___Black_spot.source: American Rose Society & Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Plant Pathology Advisory.

morphological_indicators.description: Uniform vibrant green compound leaflets with serrated margins, firm turgor, and zero necrotic lesions.

symptoms: Lustrous, deep green pinnately compound leaflets with sharp serrations
Firm turgor with intact glossy waxy cuticle
Vigorous apical shoot growth with healthy red-tinted juvenile leaves and flower buds
Complete absence of necrotic spots, powdery mildew, or rust pustules
Rose___healthy.causes: Optimal nutrition, adequate soil drainage (pH 6.0–6.8), good sunlight exposure (minimum 6 hours daily), and clean canopy ventilation.
cultural_management: Maintain 5–7 cm wood chip or pine needle mulch keeping mulch 10 cm away from main root crown
Fertilize with balanced rose food (e.g. 10-15-10 or organic bone meal + fish hydrolysate) during active flowering
Deadhead spent blooms above the nearest 5-leaflet leaf to channel plant energy into new flowering canes
Ensure minimum 60–90 cm spacing between bushes for continuous air movement
organic_remedies: Preventive monthly spray of seaweed kelp extract and silica to toughen leaf cuticles against fungal spores
Maintain beneficial predatory mites and ladybugs in garden canopy

ornamental_care.petal_safety: Maintain regular watering without foliar wetting.
ornamental_care.winter_sanitation: Apply dormant lime-sulfur or copper spray during winter dormancy after pruning.

Rose___healthy.tank_mix: No chemical intervention needed. Maintain routine horticultural care.
Rose___healthy.source: Royal Horticultural Society & UC Master Gardener Rose Guidelines.

morphological_indicators.description: Characteristic brown to dark brown circular lesions with prominent alternating concentric rings resembling a target board or bullseye.

symptoms: Dark brown circular lesions with distinct alternating concentric rings ('bullseye' target pattern)
Lesions initiate on older, lower foliage and progress acropetally up the vine
Prominent chlorotic yellow halos surround expanding necrotic lesions
Severe foliar blighting causes defoliation and exposes developing tomatoes to sunscald
Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Airborne fungal conidia of Alternaria solani. Favored by warm temperatures (24–29°C) and alternating wet/dry cycles with morning dew.
cultural_management: Prune the lower 30–45 cm of vine foliage to eliminate soil splash contact
Mulch soil bed with straw or UV-reflective plastic mulch to block soilborne spore splash
Stake and trellis vines vertically to optimize canopy drying time
Rotate fields away from solanaceous crops (tomato, potato, pepper, eggplant) for at least 3 years
organic_remedies: Spray bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma harzianum every 7–10 days
Apply cold-pressed neem oil (5 ml/L water) emulsified with mild potassium soap

chemical_remedies.name: Chlorothalonil (e.g., Bravo Weather Stik 720 SC)
chemical_remedies.phi: 0 days (Can harvest immediately up to day of application)
chemical_remedies.role: Forms protective contact barrier on foliage; inhibits multiple fungal respiratory enzymes.

chemical_remedies.name: Difenoconazole (e.g., Score 250 EC)
chemical_remedies.phi: 7 days (Strict pre-harvest interval before picking tomatoes)
chemical_remedies.role: Curative systemic triazole; halts fungal ergosterol synthesis inside active leaf lesions.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: Observe strict 7-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for Difenoconazole before picking tomatoes.
food_crop_safety.mrl_compliance: Do not exceed 4 triazole applications per harvest season.

Tomato___Early_blight.tank_mix: Difenoconazole (0.5 ml/L) + Mancozeb (2.0 g/L) combines systemic curative power with contact protectant.
Tomato___Early_blight.source: Cornell University Vegetable Pathology & UC Davis IPM Tomato Pest Guidelines.

morphological_indicators.description: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions that expand rapidly. Delicate white cottony sporulation visible on the leaf underside in humid conditions.

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-green to dark brown lesions on foliage that enlarge with extreme rapidity
Under high humidity (>90%), white downy fungal-like mycelium forms on the abaxial (underside) of the leaf
Stem cankers turn black and brittle, causing entire canopy branches to collapse
Fruit develops large, firm, greasy brown lesions with bumpy texture
Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Oomycete water mold Phytophthora infestans. Requires cool (15–20°C), persistent moisture and high humidity (>90%).
cultural_management: Scout fields daily during cool, foggy, or rainy spells; destroy infected plants immediately
Avoid sprinkler irrigation; maintain wide plant spacing for fast canopy drying
Eradicate volunteer tomato and potato plants and solanaceous weeds (nightshade)
organic_remedies: Fixed copper fungicides (Copper Hydroxide or Copper Octanoate) applied preventively before rain events
Foliar sprays of biological antagonist Bacillus subtilis QST 713

chemical_remedies.name: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (e.g., Ridomil Gold MZ 68 WG)
chemical_remedies.role: Systemic phenylamide arrests oomycete ribosomal RNA synthesis combined with multi-site contact.

chemical_remedies.name: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (e.g., Curzate M 68 WG)
chemical_remedies.role: Rapid translaminar kickback action; controls incubating mycelium up to 48 hours post-infection.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: 7 days for Metalaxyl-M; 3 days for Cymoxanil before fruit picking.
food_crop_safety.mrl_compliance: Maximum 3 applications of phenylamide class per season.

Tomato___Late_blight.tank_mix: Tank mix Ridomil Gold MZ with Cymoxanil for emergency curative arrest during active sporulation.
Tomato___Late_blight.source: Penn State Extension & University of Florida Plant Pathology.

morphological_indicators.description: Small (1–3 mm), dark, greasy, water-soaked angular spots bounded by leaf veinlets, often with yellow chlorotic halos and shot-hole centers.

symptoms: Small, angular, greasy, water-soaked lesions (1–3 mm) restricted by small leaf veins
Lesions turn dark brown to black with yellow halos; centers may tear out giving a shot-hole appearance
Blister-like scab lesions on green fruit with raised dark borders
Severe foliar spotting leads to blighted leaves and substantial blossom drop
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterial pathogen Xanthomonas spp. Spread by driving rain, overhead sprinklers, and mechanical equipment in wet fields.
cultural_management: Switch completely from overhead sprinklers to drip irrigation
Do not enter fields or cultivate crops when leaves are wet with dew
Use certified disease-free hot-water-treated seed (50°C for 25 min)
Rotate with non-host crops (corn, beans, brassicas) for minimum 2 years
organic_remedies: Fixed copper bactericides (Copper Hydroxide) applied on a preventive 7-day schedule
Biological control with Bacillus subtilis or bacteriophage products

chemical_remedies.name: Copper Hydroxide + Mancozeb Synergy
chemical_remedies.dosage_knapsack: 2.0 g Copper + 2.0 g Mancozeb per 1 L water
chemical_remedies.role: Mancozeb chemically solubilizes cupric ions to overcome copper-tolerant bacterial strains.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: 1 day PHI for copper-mancozeb tank mix.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.tank_mix: Copper Hydroxide + Mancozeb tank mix is mandatory for copper-tolerant bacterial populations.

morphological_indicators.description: Healthy lobed compound leaves with prominent glandular trichomes (hairs) and deep green chlorophyll.

symptoms: Deep green, pinnately compound lobed foliage with healthy turgor
Active apical meristem development with bright green new leaf clusters
Healthy glandular leaf hairs (trichomes) emitting characteristic tomato aroma
Zero spots, lesions, chlorosis, or wilting observed
Tomato___healthy.causes: Optimal soil moisture, balanced nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium feeding, and favorable microclimate.
cultural_management: Maintain consistent soil moisture through drip lines to prevent blossom end rot
Side-dress with calcium nitrate and balanced fertilizer at first fruit set
Prune non-productive suckers (side shoots) to improve sunlight interception
organic_remedies: Apply organic fish hydrolysate or kelp foliar feed every 14 days.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: No pesticide withdrawal needed. Produce is fresh and healthy.

morphological_indicators.description: Dark brown circular to oval spots with distinct concentric rings on lower potato canopy.

symptoms: Dark brown to black lesions showing clear concentric rings ('target pattern') on leaflets
Older canopy leaves exhibit premature senescence and drop
Brown corky, dry rot lesions under potato tuber skins
Potato___Early_blight.causes: Alternaria solani conidia overwintering in crop residues and volunteer tubers.
cultural_management: Maintain uniform soil moisture; avoid drought stress during tuber bulking
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops (cereals, legumes) for 3 years
Kill vines 2 weeks prior to harvest to allow tuber skins to set and harden
organic_remedies: Preventive copper sprays or Bacillus subtilis every 7–10 days.

chemical_remedies.name: Mancozeb 75 WG
chemical_remedies.role: Multi-site protective barrier preventing spore germination on potato foliage.

Potato___Early_blight.source: International Potato Center (CIP) & University of Idaho Extension.

morphological_indicators.description: Large irregular water-soaked foliar lesions with white spore mold underneath in wet weather.

symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions spreading rapidly across potato foliage
White fungal-like sporulation on the underside of affected leaves in morning humidity
Foul rot smell in field as entire foliage collapses
Tubers develop brown-purple granular dry rot that spreads into storage decay
Potato___Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans oomycete favored by wet, cool conditions (12–18°C).
cultural_management: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers
Hill soil generously around potato rows to create a soil barrier preventing spores from washing down to tubers
Desiccate/burn potato vines completely 14 days before harvest
organic_remedies: Preventive copper fungicides applied prior to rain spells.

chemical_remedies.name: Mandipropamid + Difenoconazole (e.g., Revus Top)
chemical_remedies.role: Locks onto leaf wax and moves translaminarly to stop cell wall synthesis in oomycetes.

Potato___Late_blight.source: Cornell Vegetable Pathology & AHDB Potatoes UK.

morphological_indicators.description: Vibrant emerald green foliage with smooth broad leaflets and zero necrotic lesions.

symptoms: Vigorous green leaf canopy, healthy stem turgor, no foliar spotting or yellowing.
Potato___healthy.causes: Healthy seed tubers, adequate potassium and phosphate fertilization, optimal soil hilling.
cultural_management: Keep soil hilled around roots, maintain uniform irrigation.
organic_remedies: Apply balanced organic seaweed or compost tea.

morphological_indicators.description: Olive-green to velvety brown-black spots with feathery, indistinct margins on apple leaves and corky scabs on fruit.

symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on the upper leaf surface with feathery margins
Leaves become distorted, puckered, and drop prematurely in mid-summer
Developing apple fruits exhibit corky, brown, cracked scab lesions
Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Venturia inaequalis ascomycete. Ascospores discharge from overwintered leaves during spring rains.
cultural_management: Shred or rake fallen leaves in autumn or apply 5% urea spray to accelerate leaf decomposition
Prune tree canopy during winter dormancy to promote rapid air drying
Select scab-resistant cultivars (e.g. Liberty, Enterprise, Honeycrisp)
organic_remedies: Liquid lime-sulfur or micronized wettable sulfur applied during spring green tip.

chemical_remedies.name: Kresoxim-methyl / Trifloxystrobin (e.g., Flint / Sovran)
chemical_remedies.role: Mitochondrial QoI inhibitor; provides mesostemic leaf surface protection.

orchard_care.orchard_canopy: Calibrate spray rig according to Tree Row Volume (TRV). Apply high-pressure nozzles into upper tree canopy.
orchard_care.pruning_hygiene: Disinfect pruning saws between tree rows.

Apple___Apple_scab.tank_mix: Tank mix Flint with Captan for multi-site resistance management.
Apple___Apple_scab.source: Cornell University Tree Fruit Pathology & Washington State University Extension.

morphological_indicators.description: Circular lesions with a tan/brown center and dark reddish-purple margin resembling a 'frog eye'.

symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots: circular lesions with light tan centers and distinct purple-brown outer margins
Cankers on branches and trunks causing bark peeling and limb dieback
Black, mummified rotting fruits hanging shriveled on branches
Apple___Black_rot.causes: Botryosphaeria obtusa fungus surviving in dead wood, fire blight cankers, and mummified fruit.
cultural_management: Prune out dead wood, cankered limbs, and fire blight strikes at least 15 cm below infected tissue
Remove and burn all mummified apple fruit from trees and ground during dormant pruning
Seal pruning wounds with wound dressing or copper paste
organic_remedies: Copper sprays applied at delayed dormant timing.

chemical_remedies.name: Thiophanate-methyl (e.g., Topsin-M 70 WP)
chemical_remedies.role: Broad-spectrum systemic benzimidazole controlling Botryosphaeria cankers.

orchard_care.orchard_canopy: Ensure thorough coverage of both fruit clusters and perennial wood.
orchard_care.pruning_hygiene: Never leave pruned wood piles adjacent to orchard rows.

morphological_indicators.description: Vibrant green leaves with fine serrations, smooth upper surface, and no necrotic spots.

symptoms: Lustrous dark green leaves, vigorous shoot expansion, healthy fruitlet development.
Apple___healthy.causes: Balanced orchard fertilization, dormant winter pruning, active honeybee pollination.
cultural_management: Maintain tree training, prune water sprouts, thin fruit to 1 per cluster.
organic_remedies: Dormant horticultural oil spray in late winter.

morphological_indicators.description: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle chlorosis across the leaf blade where yellowing crosses main leaf veins irregularly.

symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottle chlorosis on leaves that crosses leaf veins without matching on opposite sides
Thickened, corky, yellow veins with small upright leaves resembling zinc deficiency
Lopsided, bitter, misshapen fruit that remains green at the blossom end ('greenings')
Severe dieback of canopy branches, premature fruit drop, and tree decline
Citrus___Citrus_greening.causes: Fastidious phloem-limited bacterium transmitted by the Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri) and infected budwood.
cultural_management: QUARANTINE NOTIFICATION: Report suspected cases to local agricultural authorities
Remove and destroy symptomatic trees immediately to eliminate bacterial reservoirs
Plant only certified disease-free citrus nursery stock raised under insect-proof screenhouses
Control Asian Citrus Psyllid populations aggressively
organic_remedies: Spray horticultural mineral oil (1–2%) to deter psyllid oviposition on new flush
Release biological control parasitoid wasps (Tamarixia radiata)

chemical_remedies.name: Oxytetracycline Trunk Injection (e.g., ReMedium TI)
chemical_remedies.dosage_knapsack: Per tree trunk injection dosage as per label
chemical_remedies.rei: Not applicable for direct sealed trunk injection
chemical_remedies.role: Direct systemic vascular antibacterial suppression of Candidatus Liberibacter in phloem tissue.

chemical_remedies.name: Imidacloprid (Psyllid Vector Control)
chemical_remedies.dosage_knapsack: Soil drench or foliar spray as per product label
chemical_remedies.role: Systemic insecticide to eliminate the Asian citrus psyllid vector.

orchard_care.phi_notice: Follow quarantine guidelines; trunk injections require strict adherence to harvest intervals.
orchard_care.orchard_canopy: Calibrate sprayers targeting young tender leaf flush where psyllids feed.
orchard_care.pruning_hygiene: Disinfect tree pruners with 20% household bleach between trees.

Citrus___Citrus_greening.tank_mix: Foliar nutritional sprays (Zinc, Manganese, Iron) combined with psyllid insecticide.
Citrus___Citrus_greening.source: University of Florida IFAS Citrus Research & USDA APHIS Plant Protection.

morphological_indicators.description: Thick, leathery, glossy dark-green leaves with winged petioles and zero blotchy mottling.

symptoms: Dark green glossy leathery foliage, winged petioles, uniform leaf color without chlorotic mottle.
Citrus___healthy.causes: Optimal citrus micronutrient fertilization, drip irrigation, absence of psyllid vectors.
cultural_management: Apply balanced citrus fertilizer with zinc and iron, maintain weed-free tree basins.
organic_remedies: Preventive neem or horticultural oil spray on emerging flush.

morphological_indicators.description: Small, water-soaked, angular spots restricted by veinlets on pepper leaves and blistered fruit warts.

symptoms: Small (2–5 mm) circular to angular water-soaked lesions on pepper leaves
Lesions turn brown with pale centers and dark margins, causing widespread leaf yellowing and defoliation
Sunken, rough, raised scab-like spots on green pepper fruit
Premature leaf drop exposing pepper fruit to sunscald
Pepper___Bacterial_spot.causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria favored by warm (24–30°C) rainy weather.
cultural_management: Use certified disease-free treated seed and resistant pepper varieties
Do not handle plants or cultivate pepper rows while foliage is wet
Eliminate overhead sprinkler irrigation in favor of drip lines
organic_remedies: Copper Hydroxide bactericide + Bacillus subtilis sprays.

chemical_remedies.name: Copper Hydroxide + Mancozeb (e.g., Kocide 3000 + Dithane)
chemical_remedies.dosage_knapsack: 2.0 g Copper + 2.0 g Mancozeb per 1 L water
chemical_remedies.role: Synergistic bactericidal tank mix against copper-tolerant Xanthomonas.

Pepper___Bacterial_spot.source: University of Florida IFAS & Purdue University Extension.

morphological_indicators.description: Smooth, glossy, rich green lanceolate leaves with zero spots or deformities.

symptoms: Lustrous green lanceolate leaves, vigorous stem growth, healthy white blossoms and set fruit.
Pepper___healthy.causes: Proper drainage, warm soil, balanced N-P-K nutrition.
cultural_management: Mulch soil, maintain steady soil moisture to prevent blossom end rot.
organic_remedies: Foliar calcium and compost tea.

morphological_indicators.description: Talcum powder-like white superficial fungal patches spreading across upper and lower cucumber leaf surfaces, petioles, and stems.

symptoms: White, talcum powder-like superficial fungal mycelium patches on adaxial and abaxial cucumber leaf surfaces
Infected leaves gradually turn chlorotic, senesce, curl upward, become brittle, and drop prematurely
Premature canopy defoliation exposes immature cucumber fruits to severe sunscald and reduces yield
Cucumber___Powdery_mildew.causes: Ascomycete obligate biotrophic fungus Podosphaera xanthii. Flourishes in dry atmospheric conditions with dense canopies and high relative humidity (50–90%) at 20–27°C.
cultural_management: Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; switch entirely to drip lines to reduce canopy humidity
Improve air circulation through vine trellising and lateral pruning to lower localized microclimate humidity
Remove and destroy severely blighted, heavily infected lower senescent leaves immediately
organic_remedies: Potassium Bicarbonate (3–5 g/L) + organic horticultural oil as a contact curative spray
Neem seed oil (0.5%) or sulfur-based organic protectants applied preventatively
Biofungicide sprays with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens or Bacillus subtilis

chemical_remedies.name: Myclobutanil (Rally 40WSP) or Triflumizole (Procure)
chemical_remedies.role: Locally systemic curative ergosterol biosynthesis inhibitor.

chemical_remedies.name: Azoxystrobin (Quadris) or Pyraclostrobin (Cabrio)
chemical_remedies.role: Translaminar respiration inhibitor preventing spore germination and mycelial spread.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: Strict 0 to 1-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) on fresh market edible cucumbers. Verify local label guidelines before harvest.

Cucumber___Powdery_mildew.tank_mix: 1.2 ml/L Myclobutanil or 1.0 ml/L Azoxystrobin with approved non-ionic agricultural surfactant.

morphological_indicators.description: Distinct sharp, angular chlorotic yellow patches strictly delineated by leaf veins on the upper surface, with purplish-gray downy sporulation underneath.

symptoms: Sharp, angular chlorotic bright yellow lesions strictly delineated by major and minor leaf veins on upper leaf surface
Purplish-gray to blackish-brown downy fungal/oomycete sporulation visible on the underside during humid mornings
Lesions rapidly turn brown and necrotic, causing entire cucumber leaves to scorch, curl, and die ('wildfire' symptom)
Cucumber___Downy_mildew.causes: Oomycete water mold Pseudoperonospora cubensis. Requires free moisture on foliage (dew, rain, overhead irrigation) and cool to warm temperatures (15–22°C) for sporangial germination.
cultural_management: Switch exclusively to drip irrigation; eliminate all morning or late-afternoon overhead watering
Space cucumber rows widely and trellis vines to accelerate leaf drying and maximize airflow
Plant certified resistant cucumber cultivars (e.g., slicing or pickling hybrids with dm-1 resistance)
organic_remedies: Copper Octanoate (Copper soap) or Copper Hydroxide applied as a preventative protective shield
Bacillus subtilis foliar sprays to suppress early sporangial attachment

chemical_remedies.name: Mandipropamid (Revus) or Fluopicolide (Presidio)
chemical_remedies.role: Inhibits phospholipid biosynthesis and cell division in oomycete zoospores.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: Strict 0 to 2-day Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) on edible cucurbits. Do NOT apply without adhering to harvest interval.

Cucumber___Downy_mildew.tank_mix: 0.5 ml/L Cyazofamid or 0.7 ml/L Mandipropamid in water with certified spreader-sticker.

morphological_indicators.description: Vibrant, uniformly green palmately-lobed leaves with crisp edges, clear venation, and absence of chlorosis or fungal mycelium.

symptoms: Uniform green leaf lamina, active tendril formation, healthy yellow flowers and crisp fruit set.
Cucumber___healthy.causes: Balanced nutrition, drip irrigation, optimal airflow, and proper trellising.
cultural_management: Continue preventative scouting, maintain balanced N-P-K fertigation, monitor canopy humidity.
organic_remedies: Preventative neem oil or biological sprays if humidity spikes.

food_crop_safety.phi_notice: Crop is healthy. No chemical intervention required.

morphological_indicators.description: Object does not match recognized agricultural foliar specimen features.

symptoms: Specimen exhibits non-crop background patterns, weed foliage, artificial textures, or non-botanical objects.
Background___unrecognized.causes: Out-of-Distribution specimen, camera obstruction, weed foliage, or non-plant material.
cultural_management: Position the camera directly facing an agricultural crop leaf
Select the specific crop type (Tomato, Potato, Rose, Apple, Citrus, Pepper) using the crop selector
Ensure the leaf occupies at least 70% of the image frame under natural daylight
Background___unrecognized.tank_mix: No chemical application permitted on unrecognized species.
